title: Tučepi for Seniors: Accessibility Guide 2027
metaDescription: Senior travel guide to Tučepi, Croatia: flat promenade, wheelchair-friendly hotels, transfers from Split Airport, beaches, hills and practical tips for 2027.
content:
## Is Tučepi Good for Seniors?

Tučepi is a good choice for seniors who prefer calm over nightlife. The village sits directly south of Makarska and is linked to it by a continuous beach promenade. It is quieter and more residential than Makarska, with hotels and apartments right on the beach. The main weakness is terrain: the old village and many apartments sit on slopes above the coast road, so location matters more than anything else when booking.

## Getting to Tučepi from Split Airport

Split Airport is about 82 km by road, a drive of roughly 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes depending on traffic. No direct bus runs from the airport to Tučepi. By public transport, travelers must take the shuttle to Split bus station, then a coach toward Makarska. The coach journey takes 1 to 1.5 hours and fares are roughly €8–14. Total journey time is 2.5 to 3 hours with luggage handling at each change.

For anyone with limited mobility, a pre-booked private transfer or hotel transfer is the better option. Bluesun hotels (Alga, Neptun and others) offer transport from any airport to Tučepi. Dubrovnik Airport is about twice as far.

## The Promenade: Flat, Shaded and Long

The seafront promenade runs along the whole beach and is largely covered by pine trees, which gives shade in July and August. It is the main route for seniors: cafés, konobas, souvenir shops and benches line the central section, and walking is flat. The marina area and the harbor are at the village center. Evening walks are the popular routine, and the lighting and traffic-free surface make this comfortable after dark.

**Insider tip:** Walk the promenade before 10:00 or after 18:00 in summer. Midday heat on the Makarska Riviera regularly passes 30°C from July to August, and the shade thins toward the Kamena and Dračevac ends.

## Beaches and Sea Entry

Tučepi has one of the longest beaches on the Makarska Riviera. It is pebble and fine gravel, not sand. Pebbles are uneven under foot, so water shoes help a lot. Entry into the sea is gradual in many sections, but there are no universal step-free entries. Several sea entrances in the wider Makarska area are adapted for people with disabilities, and Baška Voda, a short drive north, has ramps into the sea. Rescue posts operate on the main beach in season.

Hotel beaches with sunbeds and parasols suit seniors better than the public stretches, since seating is at hand and walking on pebbles is shorter. Bluesun Hotel Alga has an elevator to the beach.

## Accessible Accommodation: What to Know

Full wheelchair adaptation is rare. Bluesun Hotel Alga is described as not fully adapted, but it has an elevator to the beach, a wheelchair-accessible restroom in the fitness area and several wheelchairs for guest use. Heritage Hotel Kaštelet and Bluesun Hotel Neptun both state they are not adapted for wheelchair users. Booking platforms list some apartments as "entire unit wheelchair accessible"; confirm the details with the host in writing.

### Checklist when booking

- Ground floor or working elevator
- Walk-in shower without a tub edge
- Flat route to the promenade (ask for the gradient)
- Air conditioning, which is standard in most hotels
- Distance to a pharmacy and the bus stop

Blunt advice: skip apartments marked as "uphill" or "with a steep access road" even if the price is lower. Many cheaper units are on hills, and a 5-minute walk down is a 12-minute climb back.

## Getting Around: Buses, Taxis and Makarska

Promet Makarska buses run along the coast, and the ride from Makarska to Tučepi takes about 15–20 minutes. The Split–Dubrovnik coaches also stop at Tučepi. Makarska has more shops, a hospital-level health service and a larger pharmacy selection. The promenade connects the two, but the walk takes around 1 to 1.5 hours one way, so most seniors walk one direction and take the bus or taxi back.

## Biokovo Skywalk and Day Trips

Biokovo Skywalk is reached from Tučepi by Biokovska cesta and opens daily 06:00–19:00 in season. The drive takes around 45 minutes up the mountain road, which has many hairpin bends. Anyone prone to motion sickness or vertigo should consider skipping it. Visitor information states the Skywalk is accessible to visitors with disabilities, but verify current access with the operator before going. Temperatures at the top are noticeably cooler, so bring a jacket.

A guided minibus tour of Biokovo Nature Park is easier than driving for most older visitors.

## Best Time to Visit

May, June, September and early October are best for seniors: sea temperatures are comfortable, crowds are smaller and daytime highs are lower than in peak summer. Many hotels close or reduce service from November to March.

## Health and Safety Basics

- Emergency number: 112
- Pharmacies operate in Makarska and Tučepi; the nearest hospital-level care is in Makarska
- EU citizens should carry the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC); non-EU travelers need travel insurance
- Drink water often and cover up between 12:00 and 16:00

faq.question: Is Tučepi suitable for elderly travelers?
faq.answer: Yes. The village is quiet, the beach promenade is flat and shaded by pines, and many hotels are within 10–100 m of the sea. The main limit is hilly terrain in the upper village, so choose accommodation near the promenade.

faq.question: Is Tučepi wheelchair accessible?
faq.answer: Partly. The promenade is flat, but most hotels are not fully adapted. Bluesun Hotel Alga has a beach elevator, an accessible restroom in the fitness area and loan wheelchairs; Kaštelet and Neptun state they are not adapted.

faq.question: How do seniors get from Split Airport to Tučepi?
faq.answer: A private or hotel transfer is the easiest: about 82 km and 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. Public transport needs the airport shuttle to Split bus station and then a Makarska coach, taking 2.5 to 3 hours in total.

faq.question: Is the beach in Tučepi easy to walk on?
faq.answer: No. It is pebble and fine gravel, which is uneven underfoot. Water shoes are recommended, and hotel beaches with sunbeds are easier than public sections.

faq.question: When is the best time for seniors to visit Tučepi?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October. Temperatures are milder than in July and August and the promenade is less crowded.

faq.question: Can seniors visit Biokovo Skywalk from Tučepi?
faq.answer: Yes, it is reached by a mountain road from Tučepi and opens daily 06:00–19:00 in season. The road has many hairpin bends, so a taxi or guided minibus is easier than driving yourself.

quickAnswer: Tučepi suits seniors who want a quiet, mostly flat beach village. A pine-shaded promenade runs along the main beach, and hotels are 10–100 m from the sea. Bluesun Hotel Alga has a beach elevator and loan wheelchairs. Split Airport is about 82 km away, so a private transfer is the easiest way to arrive.
